thread.text:
Most 2D racing games rely on an arcade handbrake button to artificially snap the car sideways.

Real drifting is weight transfer, throttle control, and counter-steering.

So I built an endless EV drift simulator in pure Canvas with real weight dynamics — zero handbrake required. 🏎️💨
thread.mediaNote: High-framerate looping GIF showing a clean weight-transfer Scandinavian flick into a long desert corner, counter-steering through oncoming traffic, and grazing a zombie bounty.

thread.text:
How the physics work under the hood:

1. Brake tap compresses the front axle, lightening the rear.
2. Steer into corner to induce oversteer.
3. Slam the throttle to pin wheelspin.
4. Counter-steer to catch the yaw angle.

EV pack regen recharges on coasting; grass burns 90x power.
thread.mediaNote: Diagram/clip showing telemetry overlay: front/rear grip vector breakdown and instantaneous kW discharge/regen bar.

thread.text:
Zero audio files downloaded.

The high-pitched EV motor whine is synthesized in real-time via pure WebAudio:
• Pitch track = wheel RPM
• Loudness / Gain = absolute kilowatt draw
• Frequency modulation bends downward instantly on regen braking.

Dual cockpit + chase rendering in 60fps.
thread.mediaNote: Video with clean crisp audio showcasing the electric whine spinning up under hard acceleration and pitch-dropping on regen brake.

thread.text:
The entire engine lives in one self-contained HTML file.

• 0 npm dependencies
• 0 build steps
• Loads in 0.1s on any browser or mobile screen
• Deterministic physics verified headless via Chrome CDP so daily seeded ghost runs stay 100% cheat-free.
